questionText: Describe a REST API you would design for a student job application feature. What endpoints and validations would you include?
candidateAnswer: I would create an endpoint to apply for a job, another endpoint to fetch my applications, and probably one for recruiters to review them. I would validate the CV id, job id, and prevent duplicate applications from the same user. I would also check that only the candidate can apply for themselves and only recruiters can review applications.
feedback: Strong practical structure and good validation awareness. The answer would be stronger with application status flow and more detail on response design.

questionText: When adding RAG into a stable service, how would you roll it out safely?
candidateAnswer: I would deploy it behind a feature flag and start with internal users or a small percentage of traffic. I would compare response quality, latency, and error rate to the old flow, and I would keep the non-RAG path available for immediate rollback if the metrics degrade.
feedback: This is a senior-quality rollout answer with clear risk control. Mentioning data migration or indexing readiness would make it even more complete.

questionText: What is the difference between controlled and uncontrolled components in React?
candidateAnswer: Controlled components keep the value inside React state, while uncontrolled components let the DOM keep the current value. Controlled inputs are easier when I need validation or live UI updates, while uncontrolled ones can be okay for simpler forms.
feedback: Clear and correct intern-level answer. One concrete example with refs would make it more complete.

questionText: A speech-to-text transcript keeps flickering and overwriting user edits. How would you redesign the UI state flow?
expectedPoints: separate live transcript and committed text
candidateAnswer: I would stop binding the live recognizer output directly to the final textarea value. Instead, I would keep a temporary live transcript and only merge it into the confirmed answer at clear checkpoints, so manual edits are never overwritten unexpectedly.
feedback: Good direction and strong intuition. The answer needs more detail on synchronization rules and edge cases to feel fully senior.

questionText: How would you detect whether a level-based interview scoring system is too lenient for interns or too harsh for seniors?
candidateAnswer: I would split the evaluation dataset by level and compare AI scores to human-reviewed scores in each segment. Then I would look at average error and score distributions. If senior answers are consistently scored lower than humans expect, I would recalibrate thresholds or offsets for that group.
feedback: Strong analysis answer with the right structure. Adding calibration plots or inter-rater agreement would make it even better.

questionText: A deployment succeeds but the application cannot connect to SQL Server in production. What would you check first?
candidateAnswer: I would first check whether the database is up and reachable from the app host. Then I would verify environment variables like hostname, port, username, and password, and inspect application logs for authentication or timeout errors.
feedback: Good fresher-level troubleshooting answer. Adding network policy or firewall checks would strengthen it.

questionText: How would you define a practical test strategy for a product that mixes deterministic backend logic with non-deterministic AI behavior?
candidateAnswer: I would test deterministic APIs with exact assertions, but for AI scoring I would use curated examples with expected score ranges and review trends over time instead of exact equality. I would also rerun the same gold set after prompt or model changes to catch regressions.
missingPoints: monitor false positives or fairness by segment
feedback: Very strong answer with a practical testing mindset. Segment-level monitoring would make it even more complete.

questionText: If users say AI scoring feels unfair, how would you design the feedback and improvement loop?
candidateAnswer: I would add a structured appeal or feedback step after scoring, capture the reason users disagree, and segment it by level and question type. Then I would review patterns with engineering, QA, and data to prioritize the highest-impact fixes before changing the scoring logic broadly.
feedback: Thoughtful product answer with a strong loop for learning. Defining a post-fix success metric would make it sharper.

questionText: How would you evaluate whether a new embedding model is actually better for this interview RAG system?
candidateAnswer: I would build a benchmark set of query to relevant-question pairs, compare recall or top-k relevance across the old and new embeddings, and also compare latency and cost. If the new model only gives a tiny relevance gain but increases cost a lot, I would probably keep the current one.
feedback: Strong junior ML answer with the right trade-off framing. Mentioning a limited production shadow test would improve it.

questionText: A file upload endpoint works locally but fails intermittently in staging. How would you narrow down the problem?
candidateAnswer: I would check the logs and compare staging with local.
feedback: The answer is too short and generic. It shows the right direction but lacks the structured troubleshooting depth expected at junior level.
